---
title: "A2 self-check — Energy and temperature"
---

Try each explanation before opening the answer. Use the [tutorial](index.qmd)
for definitions and worked examples.

## 1. Are digestion, absorption and cellular ATP production the same process?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

No. Digestion makes smaller molecules available, absorption moves material
across an epithelial barrier, and cellular metabolism transforms fuels and
supplies ATP. A complete account connects these processes rather than merging them.
:::

## 2. Intake is 100 kJ day⁻¹; losses are 20 faecal, 5 excreted and 80 metabolic. What is retained?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

$100-20-5-80=-5$ kJ day⁻¹. The animal draws down retained stores in this
simplified budget. It has not created negative energy, and the calculation
does not diagnose which nutrient may be limiting.
:::

## 3. A 0.10 L chamber loses 0.20 mg L⁻¹ oxygen in 5 min. What is its apparent rate before blank correction?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

The amount decline is $0.10\times0.20=0.020$ mg; dividing by 5 min gives
0.0040 mg min⁻¹. Concentration decline alone is not the amount consumed.
An appropriate blank and the protocol's other assumptions still need checking.
:::

## 4. Does dividing oxygen consumption by body mass remove every size effect?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

No. It gives a mass-specific rate, but metabolic rate need not scale linearly
with mass. Activity, temperature, feeding state and design can also differ.
Normalisation is a stated calculation, not a guarantee of comparability.
:::

## 5. Must an ectotherm have no temperature regulation?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

No. An ectotherm can select microhabitats, bask or change behaviour. Ectothermy
describes major heat sources; it is not identical to uncontrolled body-temperature
variation. Endotherms can also allow body temperature to vary.
:::

## 6. A rate doubles from 10 to 20 °C. May we assume it doubles every further 10 °C?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

The measured $Q_{10}$ is 2 for that interval. Extrapolation can fail as
conditions, physiology or thermal limits change. Acclimation, activity and
feeding state must be considered before comparisons.
:::
